title: Cooling tower circulating-water loop
goal: A utility engineer can trace circulation, basin makeup and blowdown, and the cold-water temperature loop.

rubric.must: The basin, circulating pumps, process cooler, and cooling tower form a visible circulating-water path.
LT-601 and LIC-601 visibly connect to LV-601, which is visibly piped from MakeupWater to the basin.
AT-601 and AIC-601 visibly connect to AV-601 on the basin blowdown line.
TT-601, TIC-601, and TV-601 form a readable temperature-control loop.
LV-601 and AV-601 visibly show FC, while TV-601 visibly shows FO.
P-601A and P-601B are visibly labelled as circulating and standby pumps.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: Direct visual inspection confirms the P-601B “Standby Circulating Pump” description sits across the horizontal footer divider. The text remains decipherable, but the overlap should be corrected before accepting this as a clean reference target. Required process paths remain traceable.

items.evidence: A visible closed path connects B-601 through parallel P-601A/P-601B branches, E-601, the warm-water return to CT-601, and the cold-water return to B-601.
MakeupWater is visibly piped through FC valve LV-601 to B-601; LT-601 connects to the basin and electrically to LIC-601, whose pneumatic line reaches LV-601.
The DN25 basin blowdown line visibly passes through FC valve AV-601; AT-601 connects from the basin to AIC-601, whose pneumatic command reaches AV-601.
TT-601 visibly measures at E-601 and connects electrically to TIC-601; TIC-601 shows SP 30 °C and a pneumatic connection to TV-601.
LV-601 and AV-601 each visibly show FC, while TV-601 visibly shows FO.
P-601A is visibly labelled Circulating Pump and P-601B is visibly labelled Standby Circulating Pump.
